quote: And we again find that participants’ feeling of knowing their partner significantly mediated the effect of information on participants’ beliefs that their partners would detect their lies (indirect effect = 4.18, bias-corrected 95% confidence interval = [1.64, 7.35]).
reason: The Supplementary Information for Shah & LaForest (2022, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-022-04452-3) uniquely identifies the Experiment 2A mediation analysis restricted to the 228 participants who passed the suspicion check (believing they were connected to another participant) and reports indirect effect = 4.18 (95% CI [1.64, 7.35]), while the shipped 3.83 does not appear in the supplied text. Because the requested metric is b (unstd) but the source only prints an indirect effect without specifying the mediation model parameterization or unstandardized path b coefficient needed to establish metric equivalence or a reproducible transformation, the comparison is not_comparable and es_value_o is undeterminable.
